steps.10: For one person, or between people?

nodes.label: What should we build?
nodes.note: A project that helps the job search and could become a product of its own. Where to begin?

nodes.label: FitLoop for garment samples
nodes.note: Helps small fashion brands keep track of changes to their samples. Ranked the first choice.

nodes.label: LessonPulse
nodes.note: Helps kids’ coding schools follow each course. Paused, but still on the tree.

nodes.label: SustainTrace
nodes.note: Helps factories clean their data, trace errors and write reports. Its workflow shape lives on in the engine.

nodes.label: AzureSpend Guard
nodes.note: Turns an existing Azure project into a tool for reading cloud costs.

nodes.label: AccessSafe
nodes.note: An existing Azure permissions project: spot the risk, ask, review, apply.

nodes.label: One workflow engine
nodes.note: These projects share one shape: feedback, revision, review, sign-off.

nodes.label: Collaboration as evolution
nodes.note: People working together start in disorder. They talk, try and fail, and order grows out of it.

nodes.label: Variation · selection · retention
nodes.note: Campbell’s blind variation and selective retention; Popper’s trial and error.

nodes.label: Retention is the heart
nodes.note: Dawkins’s cumulative selection: order builds up step by step, and what matters is keeping each step.

nodes.label: AI speeds up collaboration
nodes.note: While a group talks to each other, each person is also talking to an AI.

nodes.label: A general AI group chat
nodes.note: The giants are already building AI group chats. No chance head-on.

nodes.label: Private channels, shared view
nodes.note: Like the Delphi method: everyone first thinks alone with an AI, then the thinking is gathered for the team.

nodes.label: AI as a thermostat
nodes.note: Run hot early to spread out, cool down later to converge, and keep everything along the way.

nodes.label: A Wizard of Oz test
nodes.note: Before any code, a person plays the AI to see whether the structure helps at all.

nodes.label: Thesis: LLMs and decisions
nodes.note: The master’s thesis starting in January could become the product’s research core.

nodes.label: Making unspoken progress visible
nodes.note: Show the vague, hard-to-name, sudden progress inside a team’s work.

nodes.label: A click and three warnings
nodes.note: Simon’s safe that clicks when a number is right. Three warnings: don’t converge too fast, don’t expose individuals, don’t force consensus.

nodes.label: Mapping disagreement
nodes.note: Is a disagreement about facts, about inferences, or about how much each value weighs?

nodes.label: Two AI layers and an idea graph
nodes.note: A personal AI and a team AI, with a traceable web of ideas between them.

nodes.label: A scientific prompt method
nodes.note: A method built from philosophy and several sciences, one any large model can follow.

nodes.label: A collaboration protocol
nodes.note: A prompt is only one layer. It also needs memory, permissions, timing and an interface.

nodes.label: A GRAIL baseline experiment
nodes.note: On hidden-information tasks, can it beat the decisions of a GPT-4o moderator?

nodes.label: An evolving tree of ideas
nodes.note: Ideas branch, grow and rest like living things, and they can also merge.

nodes.label: A tree that merges
nodes.note: A Y chromosome only branches; ideas recombine. So underneath, it is a directed acyclic graph.

nodes.label: Website, agent and skill
nodes.note: The website is the garden, the agent the gardener, the skill the gardening manual, MCP the garden gate.

nodes.label: Stage 0: a skill
nodes.note: Conversations go in; the idea graph and this tree come out.

nodes.label: Build the garden with Lovable
nodes.note: Sign-in, rooms and the database go to Lovable; the tree is its own component.

nodes.label: Ramus or Stam?
nodes.note: Ramus is Latin for branch, stam Swedish for trunk. One has to be chosen.

nodes.label: The garden takes shape
nodes.note: The idea graph is the tree, the website the garden, the agent the gardener, the skill the manual.

nodes.label: The Lovable prompt kit
nodes.note: The discussion, Simon’s ideas and the clicks, turned into prompts ready to build from.

nodes.label: A personal thought garden
nodes.note: The first user would be yourself, keeping each day’s thinking with AI. Not taken, but it stays on the tree.

nodes.label: Trust in people
nodes.note: People keep making new things, and people make the final call. Ramus is for work between people; AI is only the gardener.

nodes.label: The gardener does not plant
nodes.note: The AI adds no ideas of its own. It records, sorts, reminds and asks.
